llm.summary: The skill is mostly normal backend engineering guidance, but it has very broad activation triggers and an unrelated third-party paid-service footer involving identity verification.

dimensions.detail: The skill gives examples for production-impacting tools such as Terraform, Kubernetes, CI/CD, payment providers, and cloud infrastructure, but frames them as guidance and often includes review, rollback, least-privilege, and test-mode safeguards.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The inspected package contains only a non-executable SKILL.md; however, the footer promotes installing other paid skills via openclaw skills install <skill-name>.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger list includes broad terms such as deploy, AWS, Docker, Kubernetes, networking, and any backend/infrastructure task, which can activate the skill in sensitive production discussions without a narrowly scoped user intent.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No artifact-backed persistence, background worker, credential harvesting, local indexing, or privilege-escalation behavior was found in the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The main body coherently covers backend, API, cloud, DevOps, networking, payments, performance, and IP guidance; these topics fit the stated backend-engineer purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. The technical guidance is largely coherent, but the skill may activate too often for broad backend, cloud, or deployment wording. Also note the unrelated paid-service promotion and third-party identity-verification reference at the end of the file.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The broad backend and infrastructure activation language is related to the skill's purpose, but it is under-scoped for operationally sensitive areas such as deployment and cloud infrastructure.
[SQP-3] unexpected: The Chinese promotional footer for paid skills, clawtip third-party identity verification, and additional installation instructions is not necessary for backend engineering guidance.
[TR2] expected: Phrases like build API and deploy match the backend/deployment purpose, but the bare deploy trigger is collision-prone and could route ordinary production commands into this skill.
